title: Support read-only export and workspace projection for tracker-none documentation bundles
summary: Support read-only export and workspace projection for tracker-none documentation bundles
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

In a fresh disposable Git repository:
  lore init --yes --tracker none
  lore new reference Peer --summary "Documentation-only bundle" --json
  lore sync
  lore validate --strict --json
  lore export --json
Observed: strict validation succeeds, but export exits 6 with "this bundle has issue-tracker coupling disabled". An explicit workspace member using tracker none also fails workspace validation; initializing/selecting Quest for the same member succeeds.
Expected: read-only documentation export/projection represents an empty task set for a valid docs-only bundle. Tracker-dependent writes may still reject disabled coupling. LCLI-343 (Done) enabled tracker-free initialization/configuration; this is the remaining export/workspace read path, not a duplicate request to add none initialization.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A valid tracker-none bundle exports documentation successfully with an empty task projection.
Explicit workspaces can validate and project tracker-none members alongside tracker-enabled members.
Tests cover these read paths and retain clear errors for operations that actually require tracker writes.

implementationNotes:
Reproduced exactly as filed against this repo's own dev build: lore init --yes --tracker none; lore new reference Peer; lore sync; lore validate --strict --json exits 0; lore export --json exits 6 with "this bundle has issue-tracker coupling disabled".

Root cause: both runExport (commands/export.ts) and the Ladybug indexed source builder (core/ladybug-source.ts's loadLadybugProjectionSource/loadLadybugProjectionFreshness -- the same per-root snapshot builder workspace/indexed retrieval uses per member) unconditionally called createConfiguredTrackerAdapter(root).listTasks(), which throws for an explicit tracker-none backend. Read-only projection genuinely needs nothing from a tracker when there is none configured -- an empty task set is the correct representation, not a coupling error. The workspace-contract/workspace-source/workspace-retrieval/agent-workspace-context modules themselves have zero tracker awareness (grepped directly, confirmed no hits) -- they delegate entirely to the per-root snapshot builder, so fixing it there fixes the workspace symptom too; there is no separate workspace-level gate to patch.

Fix: new exported adapters/tracker.ts helper, listTasksOrEmpty(root, adapterOverride?) -- returns [] only when resolveTrackerSelection reports an EXPLICIT "none" backend, otherwise delegates to createConfiguredTrackerAdapter(root).listTasks() unchanged. An ambiguous legacy-Backlog bundle (resolveTrackerSelection's "legacy-backlog" source) is NOT short-circuited -- that is a real configuration ambiguity, not "no tracker", so it still throws exactly as before. export.ts and both ladybug-source.ts call sites now call this helper instead of constructing an adapter directly. Tracker-dependent writes (lore link, defaultAdapter in link.ts) are untouched and still reject disabled coupling -- verified live: lore link on a Story with tracker none still throws "this bundle has issue-tracker coupling disabled".

Verified live end-to-end (not just tests): the exact repro sequence from the filing now runs lore export --json to exit 0 with a correct manifest/concept/edge/trailer projection and zero task records.

Six new regression tests: 4 in tracker-adapter.test.ts unit-testing listTasksOrEmpty directly (explicit none -> empty; a real configured backend matches createConfiguredTrackerAdapter's own result; legacy-backlog ambiguity still throws; an injected adapter override always wins); 1 in projection.test.ts driving runExport end-to-end against a real tracker-none root with no adapter injected; 1 in ladybug-lifecycle.test.ts driving loadLadybugProjectionSource the same way, proving the workspace/indexed-retrieval path (which shares this exact builder) also succeeds with zero tasks.

Full suite 2884 pass (6 new), 1 skip (pre-existing), 0 fail. typecheck clean; lint exit 0 (one pre-existing unrelated warning). lore check 77 files, 0 errors.

OPERATOR NOTE, recorded rather than glossed: reproducing this by hand, an early attempt used `bun run --cwd /Volumes/external/repos/lore-cli src/cli.ts init --yes --tracker none` intending to point at the CLI script while a temp directory was the working directory -- bun's --cwd instead set the actual process cwd to lore-cli itself, so the accidental `lore init --tracker none` ran for real against this repository's own .lore/config.toml (backend quest -> none) plus three new scaffold files. Caught immediately via a real test failure (test/config.test.ts's own committed-config assertion), fully restored via git checkout -- .lore/config.toml plus deleting the three stray scaffold files, and reverified (lore check 0, quest doctor healthy, full suite green) before continuing. No lasting damage; recorded so a future reproduction always uses an absolute script path with a plain `cd <dir> &&` prefix in one shell call, never bun's own --cwd flag, when the working directory matters.
